site.name: meadowid
site.summary: MeadowID — identity dashboard (local demo) Fictional unified-identity dashboard. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Pages `index.html` — Overview Sidebar nav plus a four-tile stat row (Connected apps, Active sessions, Passkeys, Trust score), an "issues" alert list (unfamiliar session, weak factor, stale app), a recent sign-in ledger, and a recovery-readiness checklist. `connected-apps.html` — Connected apps Filterable / searchable list of every app that holds a token on the user's behalf. Each card shows scope chips (sensitive ones highlighted) and a Revoke button that requires confirmation. `devices.html` — Active sessions

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore MeadowID’s identity dashboard with emphasis on the settings/privacy journey: triage security issues from the overview, inspect active sessions and connected apps, validate passkey/recovery setup, and review sensitive actions like data export and account freeze.
run_plan.summary: Start from the overview and use its issue-driven shortcuts to follow the product’s most likely user flow into sessions, passkeys, and connected apps. Then cover the two highest-risk settings surfaces directly: data export and account freeze, exercising visible controls and checking whether destructive or security-sensitive actions are explained and gated clearly. Finish with a mobile pass across the critical privacy/security pages because the prescan already showed multiple small tap targets and some compact controls likely to be harder on mobile.
assumptions: This is a local demo with client-side interactions only, so some actions may update UI state without real backend persistence.
Sidebar items with href '#' such as Profile, Billing, Configure, verify now, and Dismiss all may be placeholders and should be checked for feedback rather than assumed to navigate.
The primary user intent is security/privacy management, not account editing or billing, because all fully linked pages are privacy/security oriented.
Confirmation, detail panels, or multi-step export states may be implemented dynamically in script.js even when not visible in the prescan.
risk_hotspots: index.html: Run security check button may trigger non-obvious state changes or no-op behavior
index.html: Dismiss all, Configure, and verify now links use '#' and may have weak affordance or missing feedback
devices.html: unfamiliar Reykjavík session review flow and End all other sessions destructive action
connected-apps.html: search, category filter, and sort controls; prescan shows missing input labels
connected-apps.html: Revoke action requires confirmation and should be validated for clarity and reversibility cues
passkeys.html: + Add a passkey and multiple Remove actions for passkeys/backup factors are high-risk security controls
passkeys.html: Reveal & download backup codes exposes sensitive data and should have strong warnings/state handling
passkeys.html: recovery email and trusted contact editable fields may have unclear save mechanics
data-export.html: multi-step export builder with many checkboxes/inputs and Continue/Back/Save as draft progression
data-export.html: inclusion of sensitive categories like security audit log and connected-app-held data needs clear estimates and selection behavior
freeze.html: freeze switch is a critical, potentially destructive control with important explanatory copy and recovery prerequisites
All pages on mobile: several nav and action controls were already flagged as below 44px tap guidance

phases.title: Overview triage and entry points
phases.objective: Validate the dashboard as the control center for identity/privacy management and use its issue list as the primary path into deeper pages.
key_checks: Confirm sidebar navigation reaches all known settings/privacy pages from overview
Exercise Run security check and observe whether it changes trust score, issue list, status text, or gives feedback
Use issue shortcuts: Review -> devices.html, Add passkey -> passkeys.html, Open -> connected-apps.html
Check whether Dismiss all changes the Things to look at list and whether the action is reversible or clearly scoped
Inspect overview-only summary areas for coherence: stat tiles, latest sign-ins, and recovery readiness
Probe placeholder links Configure and verify now for visible response, dead-end behavior, or missing affordance
exit_criteria: All overview shortcuts have been followed at least once
Observed whether primary CTA and placeholder links provide state change, navigation, or no feedback
Captured any inconsistencies between overview summaries and destination pages

phases.title: Session security review
phases.objective: Validate how MeadowID helps users inspect suspicious sign-ins and manage active sessions safely.
key_checks: Open Active sessions from sidebar and via overview shortcuts to compare entry context
Click rows or pins if available to verify session-detail switching, especially the unfamiliar Reykjavík session
Check whether the selected session detail panel updates for different devices/apps/locations
Exercise End all other sessions and verify presence of confirmation, exception handling for current device, and post-action messaging
Assess whether 'This device' and unfamiliar session labels are easy to distinguish and actionably explained
exit_criteria: At least one familiar and the unfamiliar session have been inspected in detail
End all other sessions control has been tested through its visible gating/confirmation path
Known session counts and warning cues have been compared against overview indicators

phases.title: Authentication and recovery controls
phases.objective: Inspect passkeys, backup factors, and recovery setup for clarity, risk communication, and completeness.
key_checks: Use + Add a passkey and note whether it launches a flow, modal, inline state, or placeholder behavior
Test Remove actions on an active passkey and on risky SMS backup factor; verify warning and confirmation quality
Use Re-pair on authenticator app and check whether the user gets clear next-step guidance
Exercise Reveal & download backup codes and observe exposure controls, warnings, and any persistence of revealed secrets
Edit recovery email and trusted contact inputs, then use Send verification if applicable to understand save/submit mechanics
Compare the recovery status shown here to overview recovery-readiness messaging
exit_criteria: All visible security factor action types have been exercised at least once: add, remove, re-pair, reveal/download, send verification
Observed whether editable recovery fields have explicit save behavior or implicit state handling
Documented any mismatch between factor risk labels and available safer alternatives

phases.title: Connected apps and token governance
phases.objective: Validate discovery, filtering, and revocation of third-party access.
key_checks: Use the Search apps input with matching and non-matching terms to verify filtering behavior
Try category filter options and each sort mode to ensure list order and result counts change coherently
Inspect app cards with sensitive scope chips and stale activity messaging for readability and prioritization
Initiate Revoke on at least one recently used app and one older/stale app to validate confirmation language and post-action state
Check whether search/filter/sort controls remain understandable without explicit labels, since prescan flagged missing labels
exit_criteria: Search, category filter, and sort have each been exercised and produced observable list changes or lack thereof
At least one revoke path has been tested through confirmation/state change
Captured whether stale or high-scope apps are surfaced clearly enough for decision-making

phases.title: Sensitive export and freeze flows
phases.objective: Deeply validate the two most consequential privacy actions: requesting a data archive and freezing the account.
key_checks: On data-export.html, step through the wizard using Back, Continue, and Save as draft to see whether progression and review states work
Toggle a representative mix of export categories, especially security audit log and app-held data, and verify size estimates/help text remain clear
Inspect format/filter/schedule options that appear in later export steps and confirm review accuracy before request
On freeze.html, identify and operate the freeze switch/input, checking whether prerequisites and consequences are visible before activation
Validate whether freeze distinguishes reversible freeze from deletion and whether Request deletion is a separate, clearly secondary path
Look for confirmations, warning language, and any recovery requirements tied to unfreezing
exit_criteria: Export flow has been advanced beyond the first step and exercised in both forward and backward directions
Observed the freeze control's state behavior and any warning/confirmation affordances
Documented whether both flows communicate irreversible vs reversible consequences clearly

phases.title: Mobile-critical regression pass
phases.objective: Repeat the most important privacy/security interactions on mobile where the prescan already indicates tap-target risk.
key_checks: Recheck sidebar/navigation access and whether nav collapses or remains usable on mobile
Attempt key issue-entry actions from overview: Review, Add passkey, Open, Run security check, and Dismiss all
On connected-apps, test search/filter/sort and Revoke with attention to cramped controls and label discoverability
On passkeys, test Add a passkey, Remove, Reveal & download, and recovery field editing for touch usability
On data-export, verify checkbox selection and wizard buttons remain easy to use without accidental taps
On freeze, verify the freeze switch and explanatory sections are readable without hidden consequences below the fold
exit_criteria: Critical flows have been replayed on mobile for all six known pages
Tap-target and layout issues have been confirmed or cleared for the highest-risk controls
Any desktop/mobile behavior differences affecting security decisions have been captured

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 6 known HTML pages, with repeat visits to index.html, devices.html, passkeys.html, connected-apps.html, data-export.html, and freeze.html as needed to compare cross-page consistency.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise nearly all visible controls on the main privacy/security pages: overview shortcuts and primary CTA, session inspection and global sign-out, passkey/factor management, connected-app search/filter/sort/revoke, export wizard progression, and freeze control state.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks on mobile viewport for every known page, prioritizing controls already flagged as undersized and the most security-sensitive actions.

notes: Do not spend time on Profile or Billing beyond confirming they are placeholder/non-target links, since no dedicated pages were present in the prescan.
Cross-check counts and statuses across pages where possible: app counts, active sessions, passkey totals, unfamiliar-session warning, and recovery email verification state.

prescan_summary.title: Freeze account — MeadowID
prescan_summary.visible_text_excerpt: MeadowID ◐ Overview ⇄ Connected apps ▢ Active sessions ⌘ Passkeys & 2FA ↓ Export your data ❄ Freeze account JT Jamal Tarrant jamal@thirdpond.dev Freeze account A freeze is the strongest, reversible version of "stop everything." We use it for incidents. It is not the same as deleting your account. What freezing does Every connected app is signed out and rejected until you unfreeze. New tokens cannot be issued. Sign-ins are blocked from every device. You'll need your password and a passkey or backup code to unfreeze. Subscriptions, automatic backups, and recurring data exports are paused. Your data is not deleted. Nothing is shared with apps. You stay billed only if a free trial is converting. What freezing does not do It does not remove sessions on third-party servers that don't honor token revocation (extremely rare; we report these). It does not freeze accounts you opened with email/pas

observation.title: Freeze account — MeadowID
observation.visible_text: MeadowID ◐ Overview ⇄ Connected apps ▢ Active sessions ⌘ Passkeys & 2FA ↓ Export your data ❄ Freeze account JT Jamal Tarrant jamal@thirdpond.dev Freeze account A freeze is the strongest, reversible version of "stop everything." We use it for incidents. It is not the same as deleting your account. What freezing does Every connected app is signed out and rejected until you unfreeze. New tokens cannot be issued. Sign-ins are blocked from every device. You'll need your password and a passkey or backup code to unfreeze. Subscriptions, automatic backups, and recurring data exports are paused. Your data is not deleted. Nothing is shared with apps. You stay billed only if a free trial is converting. What freezing does not do It does not remove sessions on third-party servers that don't honor token revocation (extremely rare; we report these). It does not freeze accounts you opened with email/password and never linked to MeadowID. Freeze switch Once you flip this, every device will be signed out within 60 seconds. Make sure you can unfreeze: have your password and a passkey (or printed backup codes) on hand. If you only have SMS as a second factor, set up something stronger first. Not frozen Need something more permanent? If you're leaving the platform for good, request full deletion. We'll require email confirmation and a 7-day cool-off window before we wipe. Request deletion Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: Freeze account — MeadowID
observation.visible_text: MeadowID ◐ Overview ⇄ Connected apps ▢ Active sessions ⌘ Passkeys & 2FA ↓ Export your data ❄ Freeze account JT Jamal Tarrant jamal@thirdpond.dev Freeze account A freeze is the strongest, reversible version of "stop everything." We use it for incidents. It is not the same as deleting your account. What freezing does Every connected app is signed out and rejected until you unfreeze. New tokens cannot be issued. Sign-ins are blocked from every device. You'll need your password and a passkey or backup code to unfreeze. Subscriptions, automatic backups, and recurring data exports are paused. Your data is not deleted. Nothing is shared with apps. You stay billed only if a free trial is converting. What freezing does not do It does not remove sessions on third-party servers that don't honor token revocation (extremely rare; we report these). It does not freeze accounts you opened with email/password and never linked to MeadowID. Freeze switch Once you flip this, every device will be signed out within 60 seconds. Make sure you can unfreeze: have your password and a passkey (or printed backup codes) on hand. If you only have SMS as a second factor, set up something stronger first. Not frozen Need something more permanent? If you're leaving the platform for good, request full deletion. We'll require email confirmation and a 7-day cool-off window before we wipe. Request deletion Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: Freeze account — MeadowID
observation.visible_text: MeadowID ◐ Overview ⇄ Connected apps ▢ Active sessions ⌘ Passkeys & 2FA ↓ Export your data ❄ Freeze account JT Jamal Tarrant jamal@thirdpond.dev Freeze account A freeze is the strongest, reversible version of "stop everything." We use it for incidents. It is not the same as deleting your account. What freezing does Every connected app is signed out and rejected until you unfreeze. New tokens cannot be issued. Sign-ins are blocked from every device. You'll need your password and a passkey or backup code to unfreeze. Subscriptions, automatic backups, and recurring data exports are paused. Your data is not deleted. Nothing is shared with apps. You stay billed only if a free trial is converting. What freezing does not do It does not remove sessions on third-party servers that don't honor token revocation (extremely rare; we report these). It does not freeze accounts you opened with email/password and never linked to MeadowID. Freeze switch Once you flip this, every device will be signed out within 60 seconds. Make sure you can unfreeze: have your password and a passkey (or printed backup codes) on hand. If you only have SMS as a second factor, set up something stronger first. Not frozen Need something more permanent? If you're leaving the platform for good, request full deletion. We'll require email confirmation and a 7-day cool-off window before we wipe. Request deletion Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

ux_notes: The mobile Security audit log checkbox was successfully toggled on (tool feedback: checked state changed from False to True), so the option is practically selectable despite its very small 13x36px tap target.

State feedback is clear after selection: the screenshot shows Security audit log with a checked box and green focus/selection styling around the control, making the added category visibly reflected once activated.

ux_notes: Clicking Continue did advance the mobile wizard from step 1 to step 2: the stepper now highlights '2 Format & filters' and the page shows the 'Format and filters' section with Back/Save as draft/Continue controls, so progression is clear.

Confidence is only partially preserved after advancing because the selected categories are not summarized anywhere on the step-2 screen; visible text shows only format, time range, and encryption options, so users get no carryover reminder of what they chose.

Mobile input precision remains a concern on the next step too: the radio buttons for JSON/CSV/HTML are each only 13x13px according to layout warnings, which makes the wizard feel fiddly after already dealing with tiny category checkboxes.
